c.t: Goodwill and non-controlling interests for a member held below 100% or acquired (ADR-0059 §9, split from T68h): the investment entry's goodwill (investment - net assets + the interest) and interest at acquisition (its share of the net assets at acquisition), the nci entry per member and period (profit, translation and other shares, each rounded once, on the nci account against retained earnings and the reserve) and the profit and loss's attribution read from its profit components, with tests by hand for a member at 80% with a profit and a translation difference (a non-zero acquisition cta among them) and one first consolidated in period 1; today a run refuses such a member (consolidation.structure_unsupported) and a difference that would be goodwill (consolidation.investment_mismatch), and run_acquisition and acquisition keep goodwill and the interest at zero. Fair values (B5), goodwill retranslation (B6), a bargain purchase (B7) and the interest's dividends (B9) are their own leaves. Not a pilot item: after the pilot unless the customer's D11 answer differs from its ⚠ planning default of the pilot customer questionnaire, to be confirmed by the customer before go-live (po:2026-11-09): the Canadian company holds 100% of the UAE company, which it incorporated, group currency CAD, so IFRS 3 does not apply and the investment is eliminated against share capital

c.t: The translation difference in other comprehensive income, with the non-controlling interest's share (accounting specialist, po:2026-11-09, B3; IAS 21.39(c), 21.41, 21.52(b), IAS 1.81B): the consolidated statements show each member's translation difference as other comprehensive income, not only on the cta account of the balance sheet, and profit and total comprehensive income each attributed to owners of the parent and to non-controlling interests; the interest's part of the difference goes to NCI, not the group's reserve (ADR-0059 §9's translation share), and the reserve stays per subsidiary for its reclassification on disposal (IAS 21.48)

Group-currency revaluation's translation part moved out of profit or loss in consolidation (accounting specialist, po:2026-11-09, B4 correction 1; IAS 21.39(c)): ADR-0042 values group currency on its own, so a revaluation's group difference is not its local difference translated; the consolidation run keeps in profit or loss only the functional-currency difference translated and moves the rest to other comprehensive income and the member's translation reserve, where ADR-0059 §7 takes income and expenses at their booked group amounts today

c.t: Acquired net assets at fair value unless the subsidiary was incorporated by the parent or combined under common control (accounting specialist, po:2026-11-09, B5; IFRS 3.18, 3.19, 3.2(c), IAS 8.8): the proportionate share of net assets is an allowed measure of the interest, but IFRS 3 measures the acquired assets and liabilities at acquisition-date fair value; T68h's book values are acceptable for the pilot only for a subsidiary the parent incorporated (no goodwill, the investment eliminated against share capital), a common-control combination, or book values immaterially different from fair values; otherwise the acquisition gains a fair value adjustment layer with its deferred tax. Which case applies waits for the pilot customer's group structure (D11). Not a pilot item: after the pilot unless the customer's D11 answer differs from its ⚠ planning default of the pilot customer questionnaire, to be confirmed by the customer before go-live (po:2026-11-09): the Canadian company holds 100% of the UAE company, which it incorporated, group currency CAD, so IFRS 3 does not apply and the investment is eliminated against share capital

Goodwill held in the subsidiary's functional currency and retranslated at each closing rate (accounting specialist, po:2026-11-09, B6; IAS 21.47, IFRS 3.32, IAS 36.10(b), 36.90): ADR-0059 §9 keeps goodwill at its group amount at acquisition; to change: goodwill (and any fair value adjustment) is an asset of the foreign operation in its functional currency, translated at each run's closing rate, its difference to the member's translation reserve (the parent's alone while the interest is measured at its share of net assets); and the system posts an impairment of goodwill tested outside it. The interest at acquisition is not retranslated as such: it moves through its shares (B9). Not a pilot item: after the pilot unless the customer's D11 answer differs from its ⚠ planning default of the pilot customer questionnaire, to be confirmed by the customer before go-live (po:2026-11-09): the Canadian company holds 100% of the UAE company, which it incorporated, group currency CAD, so IFRS 3 does not apply and the investment is eliminated against share capital

A bargain purchase posted after explicit confirmation (accounting specialist, po:2026-11-09, B7; IFRS 3.34-36): a negative residual stops the run (consolidation.negative_goodwill) until a person confirms that the assets, liabilities, interest and consideration were reassessed; the run then recognises the remaining gain in profit or loss at the acquisition date, attributed to the acquirer, instead of failing for good. Not a pilot item: after the pilot unless the customer's D11 answer differs from its ⚠ planning default of the pilot customer questionnaire, to be confirmed by the customer before go-live (po:2026-11-09): the Canadian company holds 100% of the UAE company, which it incorporated, group currency CAD, so IFRS 3 does not apply and the investment is eliminated against share capital

Non-controlling interests after acquisition, the specialist's two additions (accounting specialist, po:2026-11-09, B9; IFRS 10.B94, B89, 10.22, 10.23, B96, IAS 1.54(q), 1.81B): dividends paid to the non-controlling interest reduce NCI, with a test of a member paying one; a change in ownership without loss of control is an equity transaction, which stays out of scope and refused (consolidation.acquisition_changed, ADR-0059 question 3) until the product owner asks for it. The attribution of profit to owners and to NCI is confirmed as designed

c.t: Fix (follow-up of the simulation fix, T55g review): regression evidence and suites shown to each reader for their own companies alone. The evidence is recorded by company (cases_by_company: each company's cases and those decided differently: stale, changed, regressions) with a summary of no count, as it reaches the operation's regression_summary and the audit entry; the capture's audit entry counts no cases. Each reader is shown the cases of the companies they may access, with counts over those (fail closed: no company, no case and counts of zero; a case of no legal entity only to a reader of every company); evidence recorded before is shown whole only to readers of every company. c.t: github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 bumped from v4.1.5 to v4.1.6 (PO 2026-10-28), which fixes GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q (High), the finding grype reported in erp-server, erp-router, erp-web and erp-analytics; make image-scan passes on every image again. What v4.1.6 changes for us: ParseSigned checks the algorithm against the allowed list before it sanitizes the header (where jwk and x5c are parsed), and a jwk or epk header carrying private key material is refused; a key set naming an RSA key over 4096 bits (go-jose's MaxRSAModulusBits) no longer parses, so that issuer's key refreshes fail and its tokens get 503 once the cached keys expire or a token names a key not cached; JWE decryption checks the content key's size; parsing an RSA private JWK checks p·q = n. authn verifies compact JWS against an issuer's key set by kid and web signs client assertions with an RSA or P-256 key read from PEM; neither uses JWE, jwk or epk headers or private JWKs, so only the RSA size limit reaches them, and only for an issuer publishing an RSA key over 4096 bits (our tests use 2048); their tests pass unchanged

c.t: golang.org/x/net bumped from v0.60.0 to v0.62.0 (PO 2026-10-28), which fixes GO-2026-6860 (CVE-2026-78661, quadratic time coalescing text nodes in html.Parse) and GO-2026-6866 (CVE-2026-97045, html.Render writing raw text literally under a foreign-namespace ancestor that is not an HTML integration point); govulncheck v1.9.0 no longer reports either. x/net v0.62.0 requires x/crypto v0.58.0, x/sys v0.49.0 and x/text v0.43.0, and x/sync moved to v0.24.0. What changes for us: x/net/html is imported only by internal/web's tests, which parse rendered pages, and is linked into no binary; http2, hpack and trace (grpc, so the Temporal client) and httpguts and idna (ogen's generated server) are unchanged, and the other packages that changed (ipv4, ipv6, quic, internal/socket) are linked into no binary. In x/text, the bidi rules W2, W5 and W7 and isolate matching became linear with the same results, and bidirule (pgx's SASLprep through precis) builds its ASCII table on first use; language, message, number and plural, which internal/web/i18n uses, are unchanged. x/crypto/ssh, which sftpclient uses with a pinned host key and the host key algorithms named after it, gains ML-DSA keys (built only with Go 1.27, so inert on our Go 1.26.10), encrypt-then-MAC for CBC ciphers (not negotiated: we set no ciphers and CBC is not a default) and ParseAuthorizedKey trimming only ASCII space and tab and dropping only a trailing carriage return: a well-formed host key line, with LF or CRLF, parses as before, but one with a vertical tab, form feed or non-ASCII space before the key type or straight after the key (when it has no comment) no longer parses, and since BankChannels.Endpoint re-parses a stored connector's settings, a bank_sftp connector saved with such a host_key would now be refused when it is used; chacha20, blake2b and salsa20 gain loong64 assembly only. x/sys adds x86 CPU feature flags and Linux syscalls and constants (Listns, PrctlArg5Ptr), aligns the Linux Getdents buffer to 8 bytes and moves darwin fcntl to a pointer call; go.sum also moves golang.org/x/term to v0.47.0, which only x/crypto's own tests import. Code and tests are unchanged. Still open: GO-2026-5932 (golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is unmaintained and unsafe by design) has no fixed version (govulncheck: Fixed in N/A); govulncheck lists it in a required module only, since nothing we build imports openpgp, and nothing is to be done until x/crypto removes or fixes the package
